doc.title: Harold Danko interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, April 28, 2021

title: Stravinsky's funeral and the saved shoes
summary: Asked about his liner notes, Danko recalls attending Stravinsky's funeral in 1971 and keeping the shoes.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Jazz funerals: dirges, hot return, second line

blocks.x: So we could talk a bit about your release here. All right. You were very inspired by the “Rite of Spring” and I want to read, you said that you do fairly well with writing although it might be a chore for you. I want to read this thing in your liner notes, this is a quote: “smart ass that I am when once asked what my favorite song was by a local newspaper reporter I replied ‘The Rite of Spring.’” And according to you you saved the shoes that you wore to Stravinsky’s funeral service.

Yeah. Pretty obsessive. No I realize it was 1971 — when he passed, you know I was still in the Army and a bunch of us guys were really into contemporary music and some guys had really studied Stravinsky. And I just knew it was the passing of a great. And I mean Coltrane, I missed that one, but there’s something about Stravinsky passing that just — I said I’ve got to get in line here. And I paid my respects. And yeah I did save the shoes. The shoes were very uncomfortable. They were kind of a work boot looking thing that was kind of suede, it was from the 60s. And they were never comfortable. But I kept them and then finally I think at a yard sale I don’t know somebody got them.
Okay. They didn’t know what they were getting.
He’s walking and he’s wondering why it’s going [bangs piano].
